concept.meta.title: Concept | Andrea Bencini
concept.meta.description: Concept and poetics by Andrea Bencini: the invisible relations that give shape to reality, outward in spacetime and inward in emotion.
concept.title: Concept
concept.subtitle: The invisible relations that give shape to reality — outward, in spacetime; inward, in emotion.
concept.p1: My work begins with the study of relations.
concept.p2: My background as a data scientist led me to analyse complex systems through graphs, networks, and probabilistic models. This way of thinking, more than a technique, has become the structure of my artistic language.
concept.p3: The work takes shape through relational configurations: not as a representation of isolated objects, but as the construction of structures in which elements exist through their interactions. The work does not proceed through predefined images, but through processes.
concept.p4: Concepts such as uncertainty, emergence, and probability are not illustrated, but enacted. Each work is the result of a temporary balance, one possible configuration within a broader system.
concept.spacetime.title: Loop SpaceTime — the space that emerges
concept.spacetime.p1: In classical physics, space is a given container. In quantum graphity models and in loop quantum gravity, the idea is reversed: space is a graph of relations, and the geometry we perceive is an emergent phenomenon — the statistical result of how the nodes connect.
concept.spacetime.p2: I don't simulate physics rigorously: I take its principle — form arises from probable relations — and use it as a generative engine for images.
concept.emotion.title: Emotion in Matter — the estimate as the only honest form
concept.emotion.p1: I take the most narrated emotion of all — love — and bring it back to its matter: a chemical reaction, molecules that switch on, bind, fold. The enchantment taken apart into its gears.
concept.emotion.p2: But here the work turns on itself: I reduce love to chemistry, then to data — and right there I discover that the data doesn't fully capture it. It isn't a cynical disenchantment: it's a deconstruction that leaves an ungraspable residue. That's the heart of the work.
concept.emotion.p3: Love is too vast to be explained in full. That's why the only honest representation is an estimate: not a compromise, but the very form of the work.
concept.closing: In both cycles what matters is relation, not essence: form arises from structure. And in both, a discrepancy remains — between the phenomenon and its estimate — which I don't hide: it's the exact point where my gaze stops.
